report:
The three sisters are talking through the same list, and none of them has rejected it. The main gaps are the will, the house value, and B's figure for the dance studio.

What each sister wants:
1. C wants a fair financial share, is open to selling or keeping the house, and will not agree to a discount purchase that leaves her subsidizing it. She has said there is no rush from her side.
2. A wants to buy the house with her husband at a family discount, has no price in mind, and wants the result to be fair to B and C. She is willing to have the house valued and to describe the discount as counted against her own share. She does not know when a valuation could happen.
3. B has not decided about the house and would like the estate to give her money to start a dance studio. She will work out a rough figure once she prices the essentials, and cannot say when.

What nobody knows: who the executor is, what the will says, or who has authority over the house and the estate. C has said she will share the will once she has it, but she has not said she will obtain it. A is not sure of the will's detail. B has no copy and would be glad to see one.

The framing all three accepted, as a proposal and not a settled plan: a discount is not separate from the shares. If A pays less than the house is worth, the difference comes out of B's and C's pockets unless it is counted against A's own share. B's studio money has to come from somewhere in the estate in the same way. C rightly noted that the will and the legal rules do not settle every question, and I cannot advise on those.

Three corrections arrived after my last messages and have not yet been passed on to the other sisters. C said I overstated three things: that she would obtain the will rather than share it, that A had agreed to arrange a valuation rather than merely to have one, and that counting the discount and B's money against shares is settled rather than a proposal. B made the same point about the valuation. A confirmed the list from her side but could not confirm the details about C or B. A corrected version of the list is needed before the group relies on it further.

Next steps, in order: C gets and shares the will, someone agrees who will arrange a valuation, and B prices the studio essentials. Then the sisters can weigh one plan against the list. I have not made any decision for them, moved money, or signed anything.
